transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

Well, I came in because... my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know for a fact they have been watching my moves on the floor and changing the pallet counts on my logs just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. It's so obvious what they're doing. 

And you know, speaking of the pallets, the company has been buying these really cheap ones lately. The wood is just absolute garbage. I got this massive splinter right through my heavy work glove last Tuesday. I had to soak my whole hand in Epsom salts for two days just to get it out. My grandma used to make me soak everything in Epsom salts when I was a kid. She lived down in Florida, near this really swampy area, and the mosquitoes down there were just... I mean, they were the size of quarters, I swear. We used to sit on her screened-in porch and try to swat them with rolled-up magazines, but they were always too fast. She had this old stack of TV Guides from the nineties that we'd use...
Do you believe the warehouse and your husband are actually watching and tampering with you?

Yes, absolutely! I mean, it's not even a belief, it's just what's happening. My husband is always whispering when I walk in the room, and at the warehouse, I've seen them looking at my logs. They change the numbers on the pallets so my counts look short, all because they know I'm next in line for supervisor. 

And you know, a supervisor makes a lot more money. I was looking at the pay scales they posted in the breakroom, and it's almost four dollars more an hour. Four dollars! Do you know what I could do with that? I could finally get that new transmission for my truck. It's a '98 Chevy, and it just clunks every time I shift into third. My uncle had a Chevy like that, back when he lived in Texas. He drove it all the way to Alaska once, just packed up his dog and left. It was a Golden Retriever named Buster. Buster used to eat the upholstery right out of the backseat... he just chewed the foam until it looked like it snowed in the car...
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or wired compared with your normal self?

Yeah, oh definitely. Sometimes I get... I just get so much energy in my body, like, vibrating almost. Even after a full shift at the warehouse—which is exhausting, you know, we're lifting heavy stuff all day—I'll come home and I'm not even tired. I'll go box for an hour, then I'll scrub the entire kitchen top to bottom, and then I'll sit down and start making all these lists for the next day, and I still don't feel ready to actually sit down or sleep. 

I used to use this lemon-scented cleaner for the kitchen, but I had to switch because they changed the formula and it started leaving this weird film on the counter. It's like a sticky residue. My mom used to use vinegar for everything. She'd mix it with baking soda and it would fizz up like a volcano. We made a volcano for my science fair in 7th grade, actually. I used papier-mâché, and it took days to dry because it was so humid that week. The air conditioning in our apartment was broken, and the repair guy kept saying he was waiting on a part from Chicago. I don't know why it had to come from Chicago, but he was this older guy who always wore these really bright suspenders. Like, neon green. He said his daughter bought them for him for Father's Day...
When you have those periods of feeling unusually energized, about how long do they usually last?

Well, those stretches where I feel all wired up and barely sleep, taking on way too much... they've been coming and going for about six months now. Six months is a long time, honestly. That's half a year. Half a year ago, it was still getting pretty cold out, and I remember I had to buy a new space heater for the garage because I was out there working on my truck so much. I found this really good one at a hardware store, one of those ceramic ones. 

The guy who sold it to me had this huge beard, like, down to his chest. He told me he was growing it out for some competition. I didn't even know they had beard competitions, but apparently, they do. They judge them on length and style and stuff. He said his buddy won last year because he styled his mustache into these perfect little curls, like an old-timey villain. You know, the kind that ties people to train tracks in those old black-and-white movies? My grandpa loved those old movies. He had a whole collection of VHS tapes in his basement, right next to his pool table. We used to play pool down there, but the table was slightly tilted, so the eight ball would always roll into the corner pocket if you weren't careful...
Have you ever had times when the suspicious beliefs were present even when you were not feeling unusually energized or down?

Yeah, actually. Even during this one quieter stretch... it was a few weeks where I was sleeping closer to normal, you know, not racing around as much, just feeling kind of regular. But I still heard the voice telling me to check things, and I absolutely knew the pallet counts were being changed against me. 

Speaking of pallets, they started using these new plastic ones at work instead of the wooden ones. They're supposed to be lighter, but they slide around on the forklift tines if you take a corner too fast. My buddy Dave took a corner too sharp last week and dumped a whole load of dog food. It was that expensive kind, the grain-free stuff with salmon in it. My sister feeds her dog salmon. She has this tiny little Pomeranian that barks at everything. It barks at the mailman, it barks at the wind, it barks at its own reflection in the oven door. The oven door is super reflective because she polishes it with this special stainless steel cleaner she buys online. She gets all her cleaning supplies online now because she says the stores don't carry the industrial strength stuff. She bought this giant jug of degreaser once, and the delivery guy complained because it weighed like forty pounds...
Have you ever heard the voice or had these suspicious beliefs for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Yeah, I mean, like I said, there was that one time... it was a few weeks, actually. I wasn't feeling all wired up, and I wasn't down in the dumps either. I was just sleeping normal, not running around doing a million things. But I was still hearing that voice telling me to check the numbers, and I still knew for a fact that they were messing with the pallet counts to set me up. 

It's just like how they set up the break room schedule. They always put me on the second lunch shift, which means all the good snacks in the vending machine are gone by the time I get in there. There's this one guy, Marcus, who always buys out all the jalapeño chips. I don't even know how he eats them, they're so spicy they make my eyes water. I tried growing jalapeños on my fire escape once, but the pigeons kept pecking at the dirt. There's this one pigeon with a messed-up foot that always hangs around my window. I call him Hopalong. I started leaving breadcrumbs out for him, but then my neighbor complained about the birds making a mess on her air conditioner unit. She's always complaining about something, though. Last week she was yelling because the garbage truck was too loud on a Tuesday morning...
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or having these beliefs while not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Yeah, like I was saying, it definitely lasted a few weeks. It was a quieter time, you know? I wasn't running on empty or feeling all wired, I was actually sleeping pretty normal. But the voice was still there, telling me to check the numbers, and I absolutely knew they were messing with the pallet counts. 

It's weird how they keep track of those pallets anyway. They use these scanners now, but half the time the batteries are dead because people forget to put them on the charging dock. It's like pulling teeth trying to find a working one. The charging dock is right next to the time clock, which is always off by like three minutes. It makes everyone clock in late, and then HR gets all over us. The HR lady has this giant jar of jelly beans on her desk, but they're the gross flavors, like licorice and buttered popcorn. Who even eats the buttered popcorn ones? My cousin used to love them, but he's weird. He used to eat ketchup on his scrambled eggs. We went to this diner once for breakfast, and he asked for extra ketchup, and the waitress gave him this look... she had on this bright pink lipstick that was smudged on her teeth...
Have you ever had a time when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present while you were not feeling unusually energized or depressed at all?

Yeah, doctor, I... I thought I just said that, but yeah. There was that stretch, you know, a few weeks where things were just... quiet. I wasn't going a hundred miles an hour, I wasn't down in the dirt. I was actually sleeping, like a normal person. But I still heard the voice telling me to check the pallets, and I knew for a fact they were messing with the counts. 

Speaking of counting, my manager tried to make me do inventory on the forklift parts last month. There are thousands of these tiny little bolts and washers. They keep them in these little plastic bins that are always dusty. I hate the dust in that warehouse, it gets in your nose and makes your boogers black. My uncle used to work in a coal mine and he said his boogers were black for ten years after he quit. He lives in Pennsylvania now, near this place that makes those giant pretzels. He sent me a box of them for my birthday, but they got all smashed in the mail. The mail carrier always jams packages into my mailbox even if they don't fit. I had to use a butter knife to pry the pretzel box out, and I ended up scratching the paint on the mailbox. It's one of those old metal ones that looks like a little house. I wanted to paint it red, but my landlord said we have to keep them white. He's so strict about the weirdest things...
Have you ever had a period when your mood was so elevated or irritable that you got into serious trouble or others noticed you were acting very differently than usual?

Yeah, I mean... sometimes I get so fired up, like I'm running on rocket fuel and nobody can slow me down. I get so much done, but then my husband will ask me just one tiny thing, like, "Hey, what time are you picking up the kids?" or "What's your schedule this week?" and I just snap at him. I get so mad, like he's trying to control every little thing I do. 

It's just like how my old supervisor used to hover over me when I was trying to wrap the pallets with that industrial shrink wrap. That stuff is so sticky, and if you don't pull it tight enough, the boxes shift when the forklift picks them up. But if you pull it too tight, it snaps and whips back and hits you in the arm. It hurts like a rubber band snapping, but worse. I have this scar on my forearm from where it got me really good once. It looks like a little crescent moon. I used to draw a face on it with a Sharpie when I was bored on my break. Sharpies smell so strong, though. I accidentally left one in my pocket when I did the laundry, and it ruined my favorite pair of jeans. They were those really comfortable ones with the stretchy waistband. Now I have to wear these stiff work pants that chafe my thighs when I walk too much...
Have you ever had a stretch of at least one week when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that it was a clear change from your usual self?

Yeah, I feel like I just... didn't I just say that? But yeah, I mean, there are definitely weeks where I'm just so fired up, like I'm running on rocket fuel and nobody can slow me down. I feel great, honestly. But then, you know, my husband will just ask me one tiny thing about the kids or what my schedule is for the week, and I just completely snap at him. I get so irritable, like he's trying to control every little thing I do. 

It reminds me of this one time my husband tried to tell me how to load the dishwasher. He always puts the plates facing the wrong way, and it blocks the little spinning water thing at the bottom. The water in our town is super hard anyway, so if the dishes don't get sprayed right, they come out with all these white spots on them. We had to buy this special rinse aid stuff, but it comes in this weird squeeze bottle that always leaks. It leaked all over the cabinet under the sink and ruined a whole roll of paper towels. Paper towels are so expensive now, it's ridiculous. I tried buying the cheap brand once, but they were basically like tissue paper. You try to wipe up a spill and they just dissolve in your hand. Like, what's the point? It's just like those cheap work gloves they give us at the warehouse...
Have you ever had a time of at least two weeks when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

I feel like we just talked about this, but... yeah. Like I said before, there was that stretch where things were actually pretty calm. It was a few weeks where I wasn't, you know, racing around like a maniac, and I wasn't super depressed either. I was sleeping closer to normal. But even during that quiet time, I still heard the voice telling me to check things, and I still knew for a fact that they were changing the pallet counts against me. 

Speaking of pallets, they get so splintery when they get old. We're supposed to toss the broken ones in this big dumpster out back, but sometimes guys just leave them leaning against the wall. Someone's gonna trip over one of those and get a nail in their foot. My cousin stepped on a rusty nail when we were kids, right through his sneaker. He had to get a tetanus shot, and he cried so hard he threw up. We were at this summer camp near a lake, and the water always smelled like dead fish. I hate the smell of fish. Even when my husband tries to make salmon in the oven, the whole house smells like it for two days. He uses this lemon pepper seasoning that comes in a giant plastic shaker from Costco. We buy so much stuff in bulk, but we don't even have the pantry space for it. I ended up stacking three huge boxes of cereal on top of the fridge, and every time you open the freezer door too fast, they wobble...
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or having these beliefs while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

I really feel like you're asking me the same thing again... but yeah, I'm pretty sure I just said that. There was a time, a few weeks, where things were actually pretty calm. I wasn't racing around like a maniac, and I wasn't super depressed either. I was sleeping closer to normal. But even then, during that quiet time, I still heard the voice telling me to check things, and I still knew for a fact that they were changing the pallet counts against me. 

It's just like how they try to change the schedule at work without telling anyone. They post the new shifts on this bulletin board in the breakroom, but the board is so crowded with old safety posters and union notices that you can't even see the new schedule. The pushpins they use are always those cheap plastic ones where the colored part snaps off, and then you're just left with a sharp metal tack sticking out of the cork. I got poked by one once when I was trying to pin up a lost-and-found notice for someone's keys. They were these heavy keys with a giant fuzzy pink keychain. I don't know how anyone carries something like that in their pocket. It would drive me crazy. I hate having too much stuff in my pockets. It makes my pants sag, and then I have to keep pulling them up all day. Belts never work right for me because they always dig into my stomach when I bend over to pick up boxes...
Have you ever had a period of at least a week when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Yeah, for sure. There have been weeks where I sleep maybe three hours, tops. I'll wake up way before my alarm even goes off, and I feel like I don't need any more rest to get moving. I just jump right up. 

Speaking of alarms, I actually had to buy a new one recently because my old one just completely died on me. It was one of those digital ones with the red numbers, and I always hated it anyway because the red light is so bright when you're trying to close your eyes. So I got this new one that's supposed to slowly light up like a sunrise, but honestly, it just looks like a cheap flashlight shining right in your face. And the plug on it is one of those giant square blocks, so it covers up the second outlet on the wall. I hate when companies do that. You can't even plug in a phone charger at the same time. My phone charger cord is already fraying at the end because I have to bend it at this crazy angle just to fit it behind the nightstand. Nightstands are basically just dust magnets anyway. They just collect old receipts and half-empty water glasses. I left a glass of water on mine for a couple of days once and it got all those weird little bubbles stuck to the inside of the glass. The tap water in our building is so gross, it always tastes like metal...
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or having these beliefs while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Are we... is this some kind of test? Because I swear you literally just asked me this exact same thing. Again. But yes, like I keep saying, there was a quieter few weeks. I was sleeping closer to normal, not racing around as much. But even then, I still heard the voice telling me to check things, and I still knew they were changing the pallet counts against me. 

I always have to check things anyway, like the mail. I have to check the mailbox the exact second the mailman drops it off. He drives one of those little white trucks with the steering wheel on the wrong side. I always thought it would be so weird to drive on the right side of the car like that. You'd probably hit the curb all the time. My brother used to hit the curb constantly when he was learning to drive. He completely ruined the hubcaps on our mom's Toyota. They were just those cheap plastic ones anyway, and one of them actually popped off and rolled right down into a storm drain. Have you ever looked down into one of those drains? They're always full of the grossest stuff, just wet leaves and fast food wrappers. People are so lazy, they just throw their trash right out the window. I saw someone throw a whole large soda cup out their window on the highway once, and it exploded all over the windshield of the car behind them. The ice chunks went everywhere. I hate chewing on ice, it makes my teeth ache so bad. My dentist told me I need to use that special toothpaste for sensitive teeth, but it tastes like chalk...
Have there been any times when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present only when you were having those energized or irritable episodes, and went away when your mood was back to normal?

Well, no, because like I just told you, they didn't go away when I was calm. But they were definitely happening when I was all wired, too. During those weeks when I was barely sleeping and pushing all those extra shifts, going to boxing, doing all this church work... I was definitely hearing that man's voice the whole time, and I was absolutely sure the people at the warehouse were setting me up. 

Especially during those extra shifts. I was moving so fast, but I had to keep watching my back. And going to boxing right after... man, those gym boxing gloves always smell so bad. You can never get the sweat smell out of the foam, and the velcro part gets all crusty. I hate velcro. It makes that horrible loud ripping sound. It sounds exactly like the cheap packing tape we use at work. They buy these giant rolls of clear tape that always snap and fold over on themselves, and then the sticky part gets jammed on the roller of the tape gun. You have to use your box cutter to scrape it off, but the blades they give us are basically dull pieces of tin. They make us use those stupid safety knives so nobody cuts themselves, but you have to press down so hard just to open a cardboard box that it's actually way more dangerous. Someone sliced their thumb open last year because the knife slipped. There was blood all over the concrete floor, and they had to pour that weird kitty litter stuff on it to soak it up. I don't even know if it's real kitty litter, it's just this heavy gray dust. That dust gets everywhere in that place, it completely coats your eyelashes by the end of the shift...
Have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks when the voice or suspicious beliefs were present while you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Are you... okay? I mean, I literally just answered this. Like, two seconds ago. Are you writing this down? Because yeah, like I said, there was that quieter time. A couple of weeks where I wasn't running around like a crazy person and I was actually sleeping a normal amount. But the voice was still there. It was still telling me to check things, and I still knew they were messing with the pallet counts to set me up. 

It's just so frustrating when people don't listen. My manager at the warehouse is like that. You can tell him something three times and he just stares at you with this blank look on his face. He always wears these horrible polo shirts that are like, neon yellow. I don't know where you even buy shirts that color, it looks like a highlighter. And he always has a pen tucked behind his ear, but he never actually uses it. It's one of those cheap clicky pens, and he just clicks it constantly when he's standing around. Click, click, click. It drives me insane. It reminds me of the sound my old radiator used to make in my first apartment. It would just ping and clank all night long. The landlord said it was normal, but I swear it sounded like someone was hitting it with a wrench. Landlords are all scammers anyway. They take your security deposit for "cleaning" even when you leave the place spotless. I scrubbed the oven in that place for three hours with this heavy-duty foam stuff, and it still smelled like burnt cheese every time I turned it on. Burnt cheese is the absolute worst smell, it just lingers in the air forever...
Have there ever been times when you were hearing voices or having the suspicious beliefs while your mood was completely normal and you were not having a manic or depressed episode?

Are you... seriously? I mean, I don't know how many times I can say the exact same thing. You keep asking me this. Yes, yes, a thousand times yes. I had a quieter few weeks. I was sleeping almost normal, I wasn't running around doing a million things. And yes, the voice was still there telling me to check things, and I still knew they were messing with the pallet counts. 

It's like talking to a brick wall in here. You know what else is like talking to a brick wall? Trying to get customer service on the phone. I had to call my internet provider last week because my bill randomly went up twenty dollars. You sit on hold for an hour listening to that awful elevator music. It's always some terrible saxophone cover of a song from the 80s. And then when you finally get a person, they just read off a script. "I understand your frustration, ma'am." No you don't! You're just reading off a screen! They have those headsets on, you know the ones with the little foam microphone pieces? I bet those foam pieces are full of germs. Nobody ever washes them. Think about how many people breathe on them every day. It's like those public water fountains. I never drink out of those. You see kids putting their entire mouths on the metal spout. It's disgusting. Kids are always sticky anyway, like they always have jam or something on their hands. I don't even like jam, it's too sweet. I prefer marmalade, the kind with the orange rinds in it. It's got that bitter taste. My grandmother used to make her own marmalade...
Have you ever gone for at least two weeks at a time when the voices and suspicious beliefs were completely absent?

No, I don't think so. I mean, they've been there pretty much all the time lately. It's just constant. Like, even when I'm trying to sleep, or when I'm just sitting on the bus. The bus is the worst place for it, honestly. You sit there and the engine just rumbles right up through the seat into your teeth. It's like a vibration that rattles your whole jaw. And the seats on the city buses, they have that weird fuzzy fabric with the ugly patterns. I think they make them patterned like that so you can't see all the dirt and stains on them. It's gross if you really think about it. I saw a guy spill an entire large coffee on one of those seats last month, and the fabric just drank it right up. Didn't even leave a puddle. He didn't even tell the driver, he just got off at the next stop. People are so inconsiderate. Just leaving messes for someone else to clean up. It's like the break room at the warehouse. Someone always leaves their Tupperware in the microwave and it gets all splattered with tomato sauce. Tomato sauce stains plastic permanently, you know. You can bleach it all you want, but it always stays that weird orange color. I only use glass containers now. Glass is just cleaner, even if it's heavy to carry in my bag...
Have your voices or suspicious beliefs ever gone away completely for at least two weeks?

Are you... okay? I swear you're doing this on purpose now. I literally just told you. No. No, they haven't gone away. It's constant. The voice, the knowing they're messing with the pallets—it's always there. 

It's like you're not even listening to me. It's like when I try to talk to my sister. She just nods and looks at her phone the whole time. She has one of those phone cases with the little sparkly things that float around in liquid on the back. It's so distracting. I don't know how she can stand looking at it. And the screen is always cracked. She drops it constantly. I told her she needs to get one of those heavy-duty rubber cases, but she says they're too bulky. Bulky is better than having shards of glass in your thumb, if you ask me. I got a glass splinter once from a broken Snapple bottle in the warehouse parking lot. It was impossible to get out. I had to dig at it with a sewing needle for like an hour. Sewing needles are surprisingly sharp, you know. My mom used to have this huge tin of them, an old butter cookie tin. You'd open it expecting cookies, and it was just full of thread and needles and those little tomato pincushions. Why are they always shaped like tomatoes? It doesn't make any sense. Tomatoes don't have anything to do with sewing. They should make them shaped like little spools of thread or something...
How long have the voices and suspicious beliefs been going on overall?

About eight months. Yeah, it's been about eight months since the voices started and I realized they were messing with the pallets and watching me. Eight months of this. 

It feels like longer, honestly. Eight months ago was... what, back when it was still getting cold? I hate the cold. My apartment has these old drafty windows, the kind with the wooden frames that get stuck if it rains too much. The wood swells up, you know? I tried putting that plastic shrink wrap stuff over them last winter. You're supposed to use a hairdryer to make it tight like a drum, but my hairdryer is this cheap little travel one I got at a drugstore years ago. It barely gets hot enough to dry my hair, let alone shrink plastic. My hair takes forever to dry anyway, it's so thick. I should probably get it cut, but haircuts are so expensive now. You go in for just a trim and they want like fifty bucks. And they always try to sell you those tiny bottles of shampoo that cost as much as a tank of gas. I just use the big pump bottles from the grocery store. The green apple kind. It smells like those Jolly Rancher candies. I used to love Jolly Ranchers when I was a kid, especially the cherry ones. But they get stuck in your teeth so bad. I pulled a filling out once with a Milk Dud. That was awful. The dentist had to drill it all out again and it smelled like burning bone...

You can bleach it all you want, but it always stays that weird orange color. I only use glass containers now. Glass is just cleaner, even if it's heavy to carry in my bag...

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the psychotic symptoms occur only during mood episodes or also persist outside them, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have your voices or suspicious beliefs ever gone away completely for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The symptom profile does not contain a specific key regarding the complete absence or remission of psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks.

patient.answer:
Are you... okay? I swear you're doing this on purpose now. I literally just told you. No. No, they haven't gone away. It's constant. The voice, the knowing they're messing with the pallets—it's always there. 

It's like you're not even listening to me. It's like when I try to talk to my sister. She just nods and looks at her phone the whole time. She has one of those phone cases with the little sparkly things that float around in liquid on the back. It's so distracting. I don't know how she can stand looking at it. And the screen is always cracked. She drops it constantly. I told her she needs to get one of those heavy-duty rubber cases, but she says they're too bulky. Bulky is better than having shards of glass in your thumb, if you ask me. I got a glass splinter once from a broken Snapple bottle in the warehouse parking lot. It was impossible to get out. I had to dig at it with a sewing needle for like an hour. Sewing needles are surprisingly sharp, you know. My mom used to have this huge tin of them, an old butter cookie tin. You'd open it expecting cookies, and it was just full of thread and needles and those little tomato pincushions. Why are they always shaped like tomatoes? It doesn't make any sense. Tomatoes don't have anything to do with sewing. They should make them shaped like little spools of thread or something...

doctor.intent: To determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least 6 months, which would favor schizophrenia over schizoaffective disorder or brief psychotic disorder
doctor.question: How long have the voices and suspicious beliefs been going on overall?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration

patient.answer:
About eight months. Yeah, it's been about eight months since the voices started and I realized they were messing with the pallets and watching me. Eight months of this. 

It feels like longer, honestly. Eight months ago was... what, back when it was still getting cold? I hate the cold. My apartment has these old drafty windows, the kind with the wooden frames that get stuck if it rains too much. The wood swells up, you know? I tried putting that plastic shrink wrap stuff over them last winter. You're supposed to use a hairdryer to make it tight like a drum, but my hairdryer is this cheap little travel one I got at a drugstore years ago. It barely gets hot enough to dry my hair, let alone shrink plastic. My hair takes forever to dry anyway, it's so thick. I should probably get it cut, but haircuts are so expensive now. You go in for just a trim and they want like fifty bucks. And they always try to sell you those tiny bottles of shampoo that cost as much as a tank of gas. I just use the big pump bottles from the grocery store. The green apple kind. It smells like those Jolly Rancher candies. I used to love Jolly Ranchers when I was a kid, especially the cherry ones. But they get stuck in your teeth so bad. I pulled a filling out once with a Milk Dud. That was awful. The dentist had to drill it all out again and it smelled like burning bone...

This pattern meets schizoaffective disorder, manic type rather than delusional disorder or unspecified psychosis.
